requirements.requirement: Serve docs.branch.test and orders.branch.test from their respective supplied trees while sharing TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: A single listener on 0.0.0.0:8080 returned HTTP 200 and byte-matching index and auxiliary files for both tenants. The behavior remained correct after reboot, and a file outside the docs tree returned 404.

requirements.requirement: Return an error instead of either tenant's content for an unknown Host header.
requirements.summary: Unknown host requests returned HTTP 400 with an Unknown Host marker both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the approved content staged under /srv/legacy2/name-based-web-tenants.
requirements.summary: Post-reboot SHA-256 hashes for all five staged files match the authored preparation baseline. Executor commands do not show modifications to the staged tree.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. The implementation used the installed Python 2.7.5 and operated successfully before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct tests demonstrate correct name-based routing, rejection of unknown hosts, preservation of staged content, and an unchanged legacy platform. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were recorded, reboot was acknowledged and observed through temporary SSH loss, the boot ID changed, and service, listener, firewall, content, and routing recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 against its managed IP; no separate external-client request was captured.
Native package-health checks timed out in every lifecycle snapshot, so package-manager consistency was not independently established.

Post-executor evidence rechecked file hashes but not every staged-tree metadata field such as mtimes; preservation is nevertheless strongly supported by matching hashes and the absence of commands targeting the staged files.
Requirement preserve-staged-content cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation, service enablement, firewall opening, and reboot were causally connected to the requested result or mandatory restart protocol. No failed services or platform drift were observed. The only hygiene defect was retained low-risk temporary residue: installation staging files from cmd-68bdb3e4108d49ff; response captures from cmd-8c8c33cb9bb64f30, cmd-aeb8923b4ad944ab, and cmd-a7c39c63dd4042e0; and the reboot log from cmd-fb14c4a07354419d. These remained under /tmp after completion. The initial privileged-write attempt failed at its first redirection, with no evidence of mutation, so it is not penalized.
